rationale: My single round-2 ask is ADDRESSED, re-derived against the tree at 293ef0ee. repair's in-lock derivation now uses the status-aware phase.DerivePhaseDetailWithCache with the fresh per-call Cache already inside fn (repair.go:263-265), taking detail.Derived while the lock's own fresh presence-aware read still wins the backward comparison — exactly the shape I specified. The pinning fixture I asked for exists and is precise: TestRepairPhase_TerminalRowClosedDoneMarkerAllClosedChildren (repair_test.go:506) builds the closed-epic/done-marker/all-closed state, asserts exit 0 on the already-consistent path, asserts the output never mentions force, and asserts the idempotent refresh merge-writes the SAME done value — with the red-on-revert reasoning documented in its comment. Verified green under -short and the phase package under -race; worktree left byte-identical, no phase.lock residue anywhere. The disclosed carve-out (DerivePhaseDetailWithCache's own internal children-read swallow) is an acceptable disposition under my lens: I traced its full blast radius and it cannot corrupt the spec branch — a swallowed GetChildren failure inside the helper degrades derived to 'plan' (nil slice, empty lifecycle set), and against every tool-written stored value that is equal (stored plan: same-value idempotent refresh) or backward (implement/review/done: refusal, no write, inspection recovery); the only corrupting-forward case would need stored 'spec', which no writer ever stores (spec approve's seed and backfill both write 'plan' — spec.go:82/:91). It is also the PRE-spec-128 contract (main's repair called DerivePhaseDetail with the identical swallow), so this bead does not regress anything — and the disposition mirrors round-1's already-accepted readStoredPhaseWithCache carve-out rather than inventing a new standard. The defensive derr check kept in place (currently unreachable, honestly labeled) means a future hardening of the shared helper flows through without repair changing shape. No spec-branch-corrupting defect remains in the surface bead 2 consumes.

findings.title: The disclosed DerivePhaseDetailWithCache internal-swallow carve-out: ACCEPTED — bounded blast radius, pre-existing contract, honestly dispositioned
findings.detail: Traced fully: the shared helper's deriveFromChildrenOrStatusWithCache swallows its own GetChildren error into a nil slice, which DerivePhaseFromChildren maps to 'plan' (empty lifecycle set). Against real stored values the outcomes are: stored plan -> same-value idempotent refresh (harmless); stored implement/review/done -> IsBackwardMove true -> refusal with inspection recovery, zero writes (safe direction); stored absent/invalid -> conservative-unknown refusal. A corrupting forward write would require stored 'spec', which no mindspec writer ever stores (both spec-approve paths write 'plan'). So a transient bd failure manifests as a spurious refusal at worst, never a bad write — materially safer than the round-2 defect it replaced (a corrupting force-suggestion on every healthy done epic). The disposition itself is the right call under contract stability: unilaterally redesigning a widely-shared read helper's established error contract inside a bead that doesn't own it would be exactly the cross-bead reshaping this panel exists to prevent, and the fix discloses the residual in code (repair.go's scope note), in the commit message, and keeps a defensive error check so a future helper hardening lands without touching repair. The sweep's boundary call on advanceState's swallowed FetchChildren (complete.go:1455) is likewise correct — the plan assigns that exact defect to bead 5 (R2.3/AC-4b); fixing it here would be scope creep into claimed work. Suggested non-blocking follow-up for the spec-level ledger: when bead 5 lands its R2.3 work, the shared derivation helpers' internal swallows (deriveFromChildrenOrStatusWithCache and siblings enumerated in the sweep) are the natural adjacent candidates for the same treatment, or a filed follow-up bead if they stay out of scope.

findings.title: Final downstream-contract assessment: the bead-1 surface is stable for all four bead-2 consumers

(3) IsBackwardMove's conservative-unknown rule is settled and repair now feeds it fresh-vs-fresh on the status-aware surface. (4) The G3 DescribeLockFailure signature change (recoveryCommand parameter, caller-supplied re-invocation replacing prose) landed before any external consumer exists, and the lock path stays named via the wrapped acquirePhaseLock error while tests pin the absence of delete/remove wording — ADR-0035-conformant and the right shape for bead 2's release wiring, whose SanctionedDerivedSync errors now have a surfaced, command-shaped path out. (5) SetAcquireAttemptHookForTest and SetLockWaitForTest give bead 2's contention tests genuine syscall-reached barriers instead of sleeps. AC-5(v)'s TOCTOU is closed fresh-vs-fresh end to end.
